question: How did Australian and US share markets perform in September 2026?
transcript_excerpt: Australian shares finished down more than 3% in September, with 10 of the 11 sectors down and only healthcare positive. US shares were down only half a percent on a market-weighted basis, but on equal-weighted terms they were actually down more than 5%, with nine of 11 sectors declining. The US appeared stronger mainly because of strength in big tech companies benefiting from AI infrastructure rollout.

question: Which semiconductor companies benefited most from AI infrastructure investment in September 2026?
transcript_excerpt: The semiconductor index was up another 10% in the month. AMD and Intel were up 30% and 34% respectively. Beyond semiconductors, Dell, which produces servers, was up 18%. Google and Microsoft each gained 1%, while Meta, formerly Facebook, was the standout winner, up 27%, after releasing new AI products including the Muse personal AI assistant app.

question: How did Meta's Muse AI app threaten the business models of travel and financial services companies?
transcript_excerpt: Meta released the Muse AI assistant app, which helps people shop around for better deals. This raised questions about whether companies like Expedia would still be needed for booking flights and hotels—Expedia fell 17%. Banks could also be at risk if Muse shows customers where they can earn higher interest rates. JP Morgan and Bank of America dropped 7% and 12% respectively.

question: How long has global oil supply been below demand due to the Iran war?
transcript_excerpt: Global oil supply has been below demand for seven months since the Iran war began. Every day this continues, fuel inventories get leaner. Iranian-aligned Houthis managed to hit Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline, allowing them to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and divert oil to the Red Sea, while also disrupting Red Sea shipping and exacerbating the oil shortfall.

question: What bond yield levels have been reached globally as of October 2026?
transcript_excerpt: Bond yields in many countries around the world are the highest they have been for 15 years in Australia, 20 years in Europe, and even 30 years in the US and Japan. This is partly driven by inflation concerns, higher oil prices, and AI equipment costs, but also because growth has been quite resilient and the US economy is accelerating again.

question: What did Australia's mining companies experience in September 2026 amid growth concerns?
transcript_excerpt: Australia's mining sector was weak across the board. Large iron ore producers including BHP, Rio, and Fortescue fell between 5% and 8%. Uranium, rare earths, and lithium sectors performed even worse: Paladin fell 18%, Mineral Resources dropped 19%, and PLS Group fell 28%. Gold and copper saw marginal losses, with Newmont and Sandfire Resources each down 5%.
